title: incident-bot: correlate runbook suggestions with SLO telemetry + on-call context improvements
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: On-call runbook suggestions are often surfaced without visibility into whether a suggested runbook historically helped resolve similar SLO degradations. This PR augments the incident-bot runbook suggestion pipeline to correlate and surface SLO telemetry signals (error rate spikes, latency regressions, burn rate) alongside runbook suggestions, and enriches on-call context so responders can judge relevance faster.

What this changes: 1) Adds telemetry correlation step: candidate runbooks are scored with an SLO-signal match score derived from historical SLI windows and current incident telemetry. 2) Emits new metrics/events for downstream analysis (slo.runbook_suggested, slo.runbook_clicked, slo.runbook_resolution_signal). 3) Adds optional feature-flag gated API field (runbook_slo_context) to incident GraphQL resolver so UIs can display SLO context without changing default payloads. 4) Improves runbook matching heuristics to weight recent similar SLO signatures higher. 5) Unit and e2e tests + updated docs.

Implementation notes: - New service module services/incident-bot/src/slo_correlation.py implements a lightweight windowed SLI matcher with configurable thresholds. It's intentionally decoupled from the core suggestion logic and runs as a scoring plugin. - Telemetry is emitted via infra/telemetry/metrics.yaml and recorded using the existing telemetry client; soft-guardrails added to avoid high-cardinality tags (only include slo_id and severity). - GraphQL change: pkg/api/incidents/graphql/resolvers.go exposes runbook_slo_context under a feature flag INCIDENTBOT_SLO_CONTEXT (default disabled). - Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless feature flag enabled; existing clients continue to get previous runbook payload.

Checklist: - [x] Add SLO correlation scoring module
- [x] Emit telemetry metrics/events
- [x] Add GraphQL field behind feature flag
- [x] Unit tests for scoring + edge cases
- [x] e2e test covering suggestion -> telemetry attach -> UI payload
- [x] Docs/CHANGELOG entry

Testing and CI: initial push triggered CI where lint failed on a naming nits in slo_correlation.py; fixed in second commit. Full test matrix (unit + integration against local telemetry mock) passes on rerun.

Rollout plan: feature behind INCIDENTBOT_SLO_CONTEXT flag. Start with opt-in for internal support org for 2 weeks, monitor slo.runbook_click / resolution_signal for noise, then enable wider.

Related: ENG-9876 (score runbook suggestions by signal), SUP-4321 (customer asked for evidence that runbooks matched SLO regressions).

review_conversation: Ethan Zhao (reviewer): Can we avoid adding slo_id as a free-form tag? We should keep cardinality low.
Author (Priya Nair): Good call — switched to a fixed set of tag keys (slo_id, severity). Added guardrails and unit tests to enforce tag schema.
Lena Martin (reviewer): How do we evaluate noise vs signal? Will this increase false positives?

Author: We score candidates using a windowed SLI matcher that requires both pattern similarity and a minimum delta threshold; added tests for small noisy spikes and a config param to tune sensitivity.
Carlos Ruiz (approver): Approved after tests + telemetry card updated. Ensure rollout is behind flag — do not enable by default.
CI bot: Lint failed on first run (naming). Priya: fixed in 4b2d9e0 and pushed. CI: all checks passed on rerun.
release_notes: Enhancement: incident-bot now correlates suggested runbooks with SLO telemetry signals and surfaces optional SLO context to on-call UI behind a feature flag. Emits telemetry metrics for suggestion/click/resolution events.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind INCIDENTBOT_SLO_CONTEXT. Monitor slo.runbook_click and slo.runbook_resolution_signal for volume/drops. Telemetry emits only slo_id + severity to limit cardinality. If noise observed, revert flag and roll back using standard release pipeline.
security_considerations: No user PII is emitted. We only include SLO identifiers and severity; access to telemetry events is controlled via existing RBAC. Reviewed by security team on 2025-11-18.
migration_instructions: None. New GraphQL field is opt-in via feature flag. No DB migrations required.

notes: Observed ~8% improvement in median time-to-ack in internal dogfooding when feature enabled for support org (small sample). Will monitor before wider rollout.
